identity.title: Second-Order Smooth Planning with Optimal-Transport Bellman Smoothing

problem.claim: Estimate state values in generative-model planning with few simulator calls.

gap.claim: SmoothCruiser-type planning exploits Bellman smoothness but uses only a first-order estimator, while the role of higher-order local Taylor remainders in sample complexity is not characterized.

contributions.claim: Characterizes oracle-complexity scaling by the local Taylor-remainder order β, including the β=3 rate.
Introduces an optimal-transport-smoothed Bellman backup with a closed form, policy gradient, Lipschitz Hessian, and an unbiased estimator for its quadratic correction.
Presents SecondOrderSmoothCruiser with stated ε⁻³ oracle complexity for fixed OT parameters and explicit regularization-bias relations among OT, entropy-regularized, and unregularized objectives.

stated_novelty.claim: The proposed second-order smoothing approach uses optimal transport over action distributions to reach a cubic-remainder planning regime.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report oracle complexity Õ(ε^{-(2+2/(β−1))}) for SmoothCruiser-type planners; β=2 recovers Õ(ε⁻⁴), while β=3 gives Õ(ε⁻³).
The authors report that SecondOrderSmoothCruiser achieves Õ(ε⁻³) oracle complexity when OT parameters are fixed.
The authors report explicit regularization-bias bounds connecting OT, entropy-regularized, and unregularized objectives.

narrative_sequence.summary: Generative-model planning seeks value estimation with minimal simulator calls.
SmoothCruiser obtains a problem-independent Õ(ε⁻⁴) rate from entropy-regularized Bellman smoothness but remains first-order.
Complexity is linked to the local Taylor-remainder order, with a cubic remainder implying Õ(ε⁻³).
Optimal-transport smoothing supplies the required second-order structure and an unbiased quadratic-correction estimator.
SecondOrderSmoothCruiser is reported to attain Õ(ε⁻³) for fixed OT parameters, alongside regularization-bias bounds.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns a general complexity law with concrete special cases: β=2 reproduces the baseline rate, whereas β=3 yields the improved rate.

lessons.interpretation: A parameterized theory can make the source of an improvement legible and connect new claims to an existing baseline.
lessons.application: State the general scaling rule first, then instantiate it for the baseline and proposed regimes.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when no meaningful parameter controls the claimed improvement or the special cases are not comparable.

source_observation.claim: The method description pairs structural properties of the smoothed backup with the estimator needed for its quadratic correction.

lessons.interpretation: Linking mathematical structure to an explicit estimator clarifies how an abstract algorithmic benefit is operationalized.
lessons.application: When presenting a higher-order method, name the required smoothness property and the estimator that uses it.
lessons.exception: Do not use this pattern if the abstract does not establish that the estimator corresponds to the stated correction.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the planning assumptions, simulator model, definition of fixed OT parameters, or the precise meaning of oracle complexity.
No experimental comparisons, numerical settings, or proof details are supplied.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported rates or novelty.
